Article Title: Asian Games Medal Tally: India win 8 medals but remain outside top 10 as gold continues to elude
Article Text:
Yashvir Singh, Rohit Yadav, and Esha Singh

Eight medals, but no gold for India

Shooting and kurash add to India's tally

NEW DELHI: India produced another strong medal haul at the Asian Games 2026 on Monday, winning eight medals across athletics, shooting and kurash. However, the impressive collection did not bring any change in the overall standings, with India remaining 12th as the country continued to wait for another gold medal.India added four silver and four bronze medals during the day but could not increase its gold tally. After Day 9, India stood at 45 medals — four gold, 20 silver and 21 bronze.'The eight-medal haul included silver medals for Yashvir Singh, Murali Sreeshankar, Gulveer Singh and Esha Singh, while Rohit Yadav, Parul Chaudhary, Vithya Ramraj and Pincky Balhara won bronze.India's strongest showing came in the men's javelin, where Yashvir and Rohit produced a double podium finish in the absence of defending champion Neeraj Chopra.Yashvir recorded a personal best of 85.72m for silver, while Rohit won bronze with 84.35m. Sri Lanka's Rumesh Pathirage claimed gold with 88.55m.Sreeshankar also won silver in the men's long jump with 8.07m despite an injury forcing him to abandon his final two attempts. China's Yuhao Shi took gold with 8.17m.Gulveer added his second silver of the Games with a personal best of 3:36.72 in the men's 1500m, having earlier finished runner-up in the 10,000m.Parul Chaudhary won bronze in the women's 5000m with 15:14.61, adding to the bronze she had claimed in the 3000m steeplechase.Vithya Ramraj also took bronze in the women's 400m hurdles with a personal best of 54.75 seconds.Esha Singh secured silver in the women's 25m pistol after finishing with 38 hits, the same score as China's Xiao Jiaruixuan, who won the gold after the shoot-off.Pincky Balhara added bronze in the women's -78kg kurash category, losing 0-5 to South Korea's Sumin Mo in the semifinals.Despite the eight medals, India's gold tally remained at four, a crucial factor in the standings as countries are ranked by gold medals first.China led with 132 golds, followed by Japan with 41, South Korea with 21 and Uzbekistan with 12. India remained 12th with 45 medals, highlighting how a large haul of silver and bronze medals has yet to translate into a significant rise in the standings.
Article Summary: India added four silver and four bronze medals during the day but could not increase its gold tally. China led with 132 golds, followed by japan with 41, south korea with 21 and uzbekistan with 12. India remained 12th with 45 medals, highlighting how a large haul of silver and bronze medals has yet to translate into a significant rise in the standings.

Article Title: Brij Bhushan acquittal challenged over ‘stereotypical assumptions’ about sexual assault victims
Article Text:
Wrestlers challenge acquittal, cite ‘stereotypical assumptions’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Rouse Avenue court has issued notice to former Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh and others on an appeal challenging his acquittal in a sexual harassment case involving women wrestlers.Special Judge Dig Vinay Singh sought a response to the appeal and listed the matter for hearing on October 9. The court also directed that the original affidavit and orders containing the names of the victims be placed in a sealed envelope. It further directed the appellant to file a copy of the petition with the victims’ names redacted.The appeal challenges the August 3 order of the Rouse Avenue court, Brij Bhushan and Vinod Tomar in the case. The wrestlers have contended that the acquittal order is unsustainable in law and is based on a “manifestly erroneous and selective appreciation of the evidence on record”.The appeal has contended that the impugned order proceeds on conjectures and surmises, fails to apply binding and well-settled principles of law, and, in material part, rests its reasoning on “archaic and stereotypical assumptions” about the “expected” behaviour of victims of sexual assault and harassment, rather than on a fair, evidence-based assessment after taking into account the circumstances of the victims.The case stems from an FIR filed by Delhi Police following a complaint by a woman wrestler during Singh’s tenure as WFI chief. The police had invoked Sections 354, 354-D, 354-A, 506(1) and 109 of the Indian Penal Code.Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Ashwani Panwar had acquitted Singh and Tomar after a trial that was conducted in a closed courtroom. The two were tried in connection with allegations of sexual harassment of women wrestlers in India and abroad.Delhi Police had filed a 1,500-page charge sheet against Singh and Tomar on June 15, 2023, following its investigation into the allegations.The women wrestlers had earlier staged a protest at Jantar Mantar, following which the FIR was registered by Delhi Police based on the complaint.Advocate Rajiv Mohan, assisted by Rehan Khan and Rishabh Bhati, represented Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh, while senior advocate Rebecca John appeared for the victims and complainants.
Article Summary: Wrestlers challenge acquittal, cite ‘stereotypical assumptions’ special judge dig vinay singh sought a response to the appeal and listed the matter for hearing on october 9. The appeal challenges the august 3 order of the rouse avenue court, brij bhushan and vinod tomar in the case.

Article Title: Did Troy Aikman disagree with Ben Johnson’s call? The Chicago Bears coach faces scrutiny after costly 4th-down gamble
Article Text:
Did Troy Aikman disagree with Ben Johnson’s call? The Chicago Bears coach faces scrutiny after costly 4th-down gamble(Getty)

Troy Aikman wanted Chicago to take the points

Ben Johnson explains why he trusted the call

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Troy Aikman questioned Ben Johnson’s fourth-down decision during the Chicago Bears’ Week 3 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles. Chicago had a chance to add points after recovering a fumble deep in Philadelphia territory, but Johnson kept the offense on the field.The call failed, and Aikman made his preference clear on the Monday Night Football broadcast. Johnson later explained why he trusted the play instead of taking the field goal.The Bears recovered a fumble at the Eagles’ 15-yard line and reached first-and-goal from the 6. Rome Odunze then dropped a wide-open touchdown chance on third down before Chicago faced fourth-and-goal from the 3.Johnson stayed aggressive. The fourth-down pass fell incomplete, ending the possession without points.“I think Ben Johnson got a little too enamored about what he is capable of calling,” Aikman said during ESPN’s Monday Night Football broadcast. He then added, “I’d take the points.”That was the heart of Aikman’s criticism. Chicago had already forced a turnover and moved into prime scoring territory. A field goal would have guaranteed points, while the fourth-down call left the Bears with nothing.The missed chance became more noticeable when Jalen Hurts scored on a tush push before halftime.Philadelphia went into the break trailing 10-7.There was another factor surrounding Chicago’s offense. Caleb Williams missed the game with a hamstring injury, while Case Keenum started at quarterback. The Bears entered the matchup already adjusting their offense around the veteran backup.Johnson did not describe the decision as a random gamble after the game. His explanation focused on his confidence in the play and his discomfort with kicking from that position.“Where we were on that field, I didn’t feel great going that direction, kicking it,” Johnson said during his postgame press conference. “It just is a gut feel sometimes on those things and how comfortable I am with the play calls.”The play was designed for tight end Colston Loveland. Johnson’s comments show that he had already made his choice based on the situation and his belief in the call.Johnson also had plenty to like about the offense despite that failed possession. Chicago’s running game carried a major share of the workload, with both backs finishing with more than 100 rushing yards. Johnson said the Bears needed that ground attack to win the game.He also acknowledged one area where he could have done better as a play-caller. Johnson said he looked at the offense’s 36 rushing attempts and felt he probably called too many pass plays given how well the running game was working.That adds another layer to the Aikman criticism. The Bears coach was not simply chasing points. He was making decisions based on his confidence in specific plays and the way the game was developing.Aikman wanted the safer scoring option. Johnson trusted his call. The fourth-down miss gave the ESPN analyst a clear reason to question the choice, even as the Bears ultimately won the game 31-20.
Article Summary: Troy aikman questioned ben johnson’s fourth-down decision during the chicago bears’ week 3 matchup against the philadelphia eagles. Chicago had a chance to add points after recovering a fumble deep in philadelphia territory, but johnson kept the offense on the field. Johnson later explained why he trusted the play instead of taking the field goal.

Article Title: Parveen Hooda storms into Asian Games 65kg final after beating China’s Li Shu
Article Text:
Parveen Hooda file photo

Parveen Hooda stormed into the women’s 65kg final at the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya after beating China’s Li Shu in the semifinal at the Nishio Gymnasium on Tuesday.Parveen produced a dominant performance against Shu, securing a unanimous 5-0 victory. The Indian boxer won all three rounds. The win means the Indian boxer, who had already assured herself of a medal with a 5-0 quarterfinal victory over Uzbekistan’s Navbakhor Khamidova, will now fight for the Asian Games title.The 26-year-old Haryana boxer had received a walkover in the opening round before making a strong statement against Khamidova, a 2025 World Championships silver medallist.Her victory over Li now takes her one step closer to completing a remarkable return to the Asian Games podium, with a gold medal the only prize left to fight for.Parveen had won bronze at the previous edition, a medal that had raised hopes of an Olympic push, but was stripped of it months later after whereabouts failures between April 2022 and March 2023.After serving her suspension, she rebuilt her career with gold at the World Boxing Cup Finals in late 2025, only to suffer another setback at the Commonwealth Games, where she lost her opening bout to Sacha Hickey on a split decision.Indian boxing had returned from the Hangzhou Asian Games with four medals - one silver and three bronze.The 2026 campaign has the potential to take that tally higher, with eight Indian boxers entering semifinal bouts in Nagoya and each already assured of a medal.Parveen is one of them, along with Ankush in the men’s 80kg and Narender in the men’s +90kg category, while India also has representation in the other semifinal bouts across the men’s and women’s draws.India will have six boxers in semifinal action tomorrow as the Asian Games boxing competition enters its medal-deciding stage.Priya will face China’s Yang Chengyu in the women’s 60kg category, while Tokyo Olympics bronze medallist Lovlina Borgohain takes on Kazakhstan’s Natalya Bogdanova in the women’s 75kg semifinal.In the men’s draws, Kapil Pokhariya will meet Uzbekistan’s Turabek Khabibullaev in the 90kg category, with Indian representation also in the 55kg and 70kg semifinals.
Article Summary: Parveen hooda beat china's li shu 5-0 in the women's 65kg semifinal. Indian boxer will now fight for the asian games title in nagoya. Parveen had already assured herself of a medal with a quarterfinal victory over uzbekistan's navbakhor khamidova.

Thiruvananthapuram: West Indies were comfortably placed at 107 for no loss when Kuldeep Yadav was brought into the attack in the 16th over. Fourteen balls into his spell, West Indies opener John Campbell top-edged a tossed-up delivery to short fine leg, giving India the breakthrough they needed.Virat Kohli and Shubman Gill would later soak in the applause for their batting. But it was Kuldeep who helped India turn the game around at the Greenfield International Stadium with flight, dip and guile.Kuldeep is a rhythm bowler. In his nine-year international career, whenever he hits his stride early, he reaps dividends. Sunday was a case in point. Kuldeep showcased his full repertoire, from the tossed-up delivery above the batter’s eyeline and the wrong one to the quickish fuller delivery. He displayed all his wares to finish with 4/40 and win the Player of the Match award.“Personally, I liked my rhythm. Just varying the pace and trying to read the batters, where they are going to hit me,” Kuldeep said after India’s eight-wicket win.“Sometimes to get that confidence back you need to have a spell like this,” the 31-year-old added.For a man with Kuldeep’s skill set, it is baffling why he gets so little match time.Since his debut in 2017, Kuldeep has taken 198 wickets in this format at an average of nearly 27. Of the 10 ODIs and 28 T20Is India have played this year, he has featured in five and four games respectively.Even Kuldeep’s long-form career has been a start-stop affair, featuring sporadically in 19 Tests since his debut against Australia in Dharamshala in 2017.“Kuldeep needs to be handled with care and used as a wicket-taking bowler. The more he bowls, the better he gets because it will help him get into rhythm. We were surprised that Kuldeep has been benched for so many games. Kuldeep is a match-winner and is one of the few mystery bowlers in the world,” former India left-arm spinner Venkatapathy Raju told TOI.Raju believes Kuldeep is a master of deception, capable of taking the pitch out of the equation.“Sometimes for the sake of team combinations you may have to drop Kuldeep. But you need to use him for all the crucial games. Kuldeep is India’s trump card in the 2027 World Cup because of the variety and wicket-taking ability,” Raju added.
Article Summary: Kuldeep yadav was brought into the attack in the 16th over. West indies were comfortably placed at 107 for no loss when kuldeep was brought in. Fourteen balls into his spell, west indies opener john campbell top-edged a tossed-up delivery to short fine leg.

Article Title: ‘Nothing has changed’: Rohit Sharma opens up on his special bond with Virat Kohli
Article Text:
Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli (AFP Photo)

‘There’s a strong camaraderie between the two of us’

‘Appreciation has always been there from both sides’

NEW DELHI: Rohit Sharma has opened up on his long-standing bond with Virat Kohli , describing a relationship built on camaraderie, mutual respect and a shared commitment to the Indian cause, while insisting that little has changed between the two despite their evolving roles.Rohit Sharma, speaking to JioStar ahead of India's second ODI against West Indies on Wednesday, shared his thoughts on his relationship with Kohli and revealed how the two continue to exchange ideas about their batting and the team's goals.The pair have been teammates for almost two decades, with Rohit making his India debut in 2007 and Kohli following a year later. From sharing the dressing room to leading India at different stages, their careers have been closely intertwined.“I think we were together. This started, I think, when we were playing in Australia, or right after Australia when we came to India. That's when this started, and whenever this plays on TV, we look at each other and laugh. Which is good, it's fun. People want masala, so there you go, there is some masala,” Rohit said.Rohit said the different personalities and methods of the two batters have never affected their shared objective.“Both of us, we've almost started playing at the same time. I made my debut in 2007, he made his debut in 2008. And since then, we've been trying to give our best for the team. So yeah, there's a strong camaraderie between the two of us,” he said.“We understand what it requires to be at a certain level when you're playing at this level. Methods are different, obviously, but that's how it should be, every individual is different.”Rohit was also emphatic about Kohli's contribution to Indian cricket and what he expects from his former captain going forward.“For what he has done for the team, for this team, there is no question, there is no asking what has he done. It's there for everyone to see it,” Rohit said.“And what he is going to do from here on now, I don't think anything has changed. He'll be the same Kohli that we know of: wants to come, prepare well, go get the runs, win games for Team India.”Rohit added that the same team-first approach remained evident irrespective of who was leading India.“When he was captain, pretty much the same. When I was captain, pretty much the same. And I don't see any reason why anything needs to change,” he said.Rohit also revealed that the two continue to have conversations about their individual games, with their mutual appreciation extending beyond their performances on the field.“Appreciation, appreciation if something good has happened, it has always been there from both sides. I appreciate what he has done, you know, when he took over as a captain with the Test team, especially. It was brilliant, what he did with that team,” Rohit said.“At the same time, there has been a lot of discussion about how both of us as individuals can improve our own game. So, sometimes if something is happening with my batting, he comes and mentions it, sometimes I mention it.”On the upcoming World Cup, Rohit said there was no need for him to explain its importance to Kohli, who has already played four 50-over World Cups.“No, no. He has been playing for so many years. Whether it's the '27 World Cup or the '23 World Cup, there's no need to explain it to him. World Cup is World Cup,” Rohit said.The two may now spend less time together away from cricket, but Rohit said their connection remains unchanged.“Now both of us are spending more time at home, which is always nice,” he said.(Watch Rohit Sharma’s exclusive interview on JioHotstar and Star Sports Network, September 30)(Watch the ICC Men’s ODI World Cup schedule announcement on JioHotstar and Star Sports, October 1)

Article Title: Neeru Dhanda scripts history with India’s first individual Asian Games gold in women’s trap

Neeru Dhanda scripted history on Tuesday by becoming the first Indian shooter to win an Asian Games gold medal in the women’s trap individual event, smashing the continental record in the process.The 26-year-old from Haryana produced a score of 28 in the eight-shooter final to surpass the previous Asian record of 24 and claim the gold medal.Neeru’s triumph came after she had helped India secure silver in the women’s trap team event earlier in the competition. Her latest achievement is even more significant as no Indian woman trap or skeet shooter had previously won an individual medal at the Asian Games.Randhir Singh had won India’s historic individual gold in the men’s individual trap event at the 1978 Games, while Ronjan Sodhi claimed the men’s double trap individual gold at the 2010 edition.Neeru had entered the final as one of the joint leaders after topping qualification alongside Qatar’s Ray Bassil with 118 points. The score was also a Games record for qualification.The Haryana shooter has been in exceptional form this year. In July, she became the first Indian woman to win a World Cup gold medal in the trap event at the Shotgun World Cup in Italy.Earlier in the Asian Games, Neeru, Aashima Ahlawat and Manisha Keer combined for 328 to win silver in the women’s trap team event.China took gold with 346, while Kuwait secured bronze with 325.The Chinese team comprised Liu Shanshan, Sun Yunong and Zhu Jingyu, while Kuwait were represented by Alhawal Shahad, Abdulmalik Hajar and Alhawal Sarah.Aashima and Manisha could not make the individual final, finishing 16th and 23rd respectively in qualification after scoring 106 and 104.

Article Title: Neeru Dhanda: From tin cans and a borrowed gun to World Cup history and Asian Games gold
Article Text:
India’s Neeru Dhanda celebrates after helping the women’s trap team win silver at the 2026 Asian Games in Nagoya. Dhanda also qualified for the individual final after finishing joint-second in qualification with a score of 118/125.

From tin cans to the Indian Army and World Cup glory

From being inspired by her cousin Lakhsay Sheron’s Asian Games medal to winning one herself, Neeru Dhanda has completed a remarkable journey - and in the process, created a piece of history for Indian shooting.The 26-year-old Indian shooter produced a stunning 28/30 in the women’s trap final to clinch gold at the Asian Games on Tuesday. China’s Sun Yunong finished second with 26, while Kuwait’s Hajar Abdulmalik took bronze with 21.Dhanda’s 28 also shattered the previous Asian record of 24. The Indian had already announced her intent by topping qualification with 118 hits out of 125, and she carried that form into the six-shooter final to produce the biggest result of her career in the process delivering India its first individual gold medal of the 2026 Games and taking the country’s tally to five gold medals and 47 overall.Earlier in the day, Dhanda had already played a central role in India’s women’s trap team silver, joining Aashima Ahlawat and Manisha Keer to finish second behind China.For Dhanda, the triumph comes just months after she broke new ground at the ISSF World Cup in Lonato, Italy. In July, she became the first Indian woman to win an individual gold medal in trap at an ISSF World Cup.The Asian Games gold now gives that World Cup success a continental dimension.Dhanda had arrived in Aichi-Nagoya as the reigning Asian champion, having won gold at the 2025 Asian Shooting Championships. She also had a mixed-team bronze from the ISSF World Cup in Almaty earlier this year.Dhanda was inspired to take up shooting after watching her maternal cousin Lakshay Sheoran win a silver medal in men's trap at the 2018 Asian Games. Sheoran also lent her his gun when she was beginning her journey in the sport. Years later, Dhanda has followed him to the Asian Games podium, but has gone one better by winning gold.The rise has been backed by the Indian Army, where Dhanda serves as a Naib Subedar in the Corps of Military Police. She trains at the Army Marksmanship Unit in Mhow and works with foreign coach Peter Wilson, the London 2012 Olympic trap champion. She is also part of the Target Olympic Podium Scheme's Development Group.

Article Title: From Jamshedpur slum to Asian Games: Joga Purty’s unlikely climb to India’s speed climbing record
Article Text:
Joga Purty during a practice session and (pic right) with her coach Bibhas

Kolkata:

When Joga Purty first walked into the climbing wall at JRD Tata Sports Complex in Jamshedpur, she had no idea what sport climbing was.A friend had suggested she tag along, and curiosity brought her there. Nearly seven years later, the 19-year-old from a modest family in Jamshedpur is India’s national record holder in speed climbing and on her way to the Asian Games “I never thought I would get an opportunity to compete at the Asian Games,” said Purty, who will make her debut in women’s speed climbing at the continental showpiece in Japan on Tuesday.“To be honest, my reaction was quite normal. I didn’t know much about the Games then, and I had already travelled for international competitions, so I didn’t think of it as something very different.”The Asiad may be her biggest stage yet, but the teenager’s journey has been anything but straightforward.Her father, Nandu, runs a small shop while her mother, Jhana, works as a domestic help. The youngest among three siblings, it was initially difficult for Purty to convince her family and neighbours that climbing was worth pursuing.“Joga comes from a humble background and grew up in the slum area. In the early days, she would often miss training sessions. I used to visit her home and speak to her parents to convince them to let her come for practice,” said Bibhas Roy, who trained her at Tata Steel Adventure Foundation (TSAF) Climbing Academy before moving to Bengaluru as India’s national coach in 2024.But the turning point came when she won medals in all three climbing disciplines at a national championship before the Covid-19 pandemic. “When my photo appeared in the newspapers, my mother became very proud. After that, nobody questioned my participation anymore,” she recalled.Although Purty initially competed in all three disciplines of sport climbing — boulder, lead and speed — her coaches soon recognised where her true potential lay. “Once we realised she was excelling in speed climbing, we decided to focus entirely on that discipline,” Roy said.The move quickly brought results. Purty announced herself on the international stage by winning a silver medal at 2024 IFSC Asian Youth Climbing Championships.Since then, she has represented India at World Championships and 2026 Asian Climbing Championships, while repeatedly lowering her own national record. Her current national mark of 7.37 seconds sealed her place in India’s Asian Games squad.Ahead of the Asian Games, Purty spent two months training in Indonesia before attending a camp in Thailand. While Roy admits Purty’s timings did not improve as much as expected during the latest overseas stint, he remains convinced that her best days lie ahead.“Her biggest strengths are her natural power and explosive speed. If she continues training properly and remains disciplined, I believe she can break into the six-second range within the next year,” he said.Climbing is also an expensive sport and for Purty, support from the Tata Steel Adventure Foundation has played a key role in keeping her climbing dream alive. A good pair of climbing shoes costs around Rs 10,000 and typically lasts only three to six months depending on usage. A harness can cost upwards of Rs 11,000, while chalk bags and chalk powder add significantly to the expenses.Competition at the Asian Games, however, will be fierce, with climbers from Kazakhstan, Indonesia, China and hosts Japan among the favourites. Yet Roy believes his protégé has the qualities required to compete with the continent’s best.“She has a very bright future and the potential to qualify for the Olympics one day,” he said.
Article Summary: Joga purty will make her debut in women’s speed climbing at the asian games. The 19-year-old from a modest family in jamshedpur is india's national record holder in speed climbing. Purty announced herself on the international stage by winning a silver medal at 2024 ifsc asian youth climbing championships.

Article Title: Savitha Shri’s Chess Olympiad gold demands a closer look beyond the stunning 9/10

Savitha Shri’s individual gold medal performance (9 points in 10 games) is a highly notable achievement. Her exploits at the Chess Olympiad that concluded in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, on Sunday, however, warrant a closer look.“I really don't know what to say... for gambling the positions or keeping us tense throughout the rounds! But yes, when there were really tense moments, she was strong enough to capitalise on those opportunities. She has the fighting spirit and she is not scared of playing any position. Irrespective of the evaluation, she keeps fighting,” India’s top board player Koneru Humpy told the Chessbase India webcast about Savitha Shri.In other words, those were not simply clean wins where she outplayed her opponents. The majority of the games featured multiple inaccuracies, which is the norm in shorter time controls but not in classical chess.Veteran GM Levon Aronian told Lichess in an interview that if players want to win, they will have to take gambles these days as the level of preparation has increased. There is, however, a thin line between taking risks and being in reasonable control despite taking liberties.It is also unclear if Savitha Shri was fully aware of the dangers of her inaccuracies. Savitha Shri, 19, also played on the reserve board (fifth). Despite slipping from the Elo high of 2435 four years ago to 2382 at this Olympiad, all her rivals were lower-rated than her.Still, the value of IM Savitha Shri’s performance for India cannot be ignored. She scored eight wins when GMs K Humpy, R Vaishali and Divya Deshmukh scored a combined nine wins.Vaishali (2.5/6) was rested for four of the last seven rounds. Her form is a huge worry as she is expected to challenge China’s Ju Wenjun for the women’s world crown early next year.

Article Title: Chess Olympiad Round 9: D Gukesh channels his world champion self, overturns almost-lost game to keep India in gold hunt
Article Text:
Dommaraju Gukesh of India (Photo by Rafal Oleksiewicz for FIDE)

How Gukesh turned the tables on Donchenko

Vantika, Divya lead India's women to victory

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

ALSO READ:

NEW DELHI: Since becoming world champion two years ago, noise has followed Dommaraju Gukesh almost everywhere, at times making it feel as though he isn't worthy of the title he rightfully won.But on Friday, when India needed the youngest world champion in history to deliver a win, he did exactly that, turning around an almost-lost position to beat Germany's Alexander Donchenko in Round 9 of the 46th Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan.It was the kind of performance that felt like it could quiet the criticism all on its own.Playing black, Gukesh traded off his dark-squared bishop early to damage White's pawn structure, then spent the middlegame manoeuvring patiently, repositioning knights, expanding on the queenside with a5-a4, and probing for weaknesses without rushing.For a long stretch, the position stayed murky and roughly balanced, with both sides shuffling pieces and neither able to land a clean blow.It was in the run-up to the time control that things turned dangerous for Gukesh. Donchenko doubled his rooks on the e-file and pushed one all the way to e6, aiming squarely at Black's king, which had been forced to step out to f7 for safety.With his own clock running low, Gukesh had to defend precisely while trying to generate counterplay of his own on the kingside, pushing his h- and g-pawns forward to create complications.It was a position where one careless move could have ended the game in White's favour.Gukesh held his nerve. As the pawn storms and piece trades settled down, he found a route to activate his queen and knight while White's pieces drifted out of coordination.The Chennai-born grandmaster found an excellent move with 51...Nf4. The German sacked Gukesh's knight with 52.Rxf4, but Donchenko's bishop was thus left hanging on c3; Gukesh's queen swooped in to capture it, and from there it was a matter of technique.A check with his queen forced Donchenko's king into an impossible spot, and White resigned rather than play on a piece down with his king exposed.Elsewhere on the board, Nihal Sarin, playing white, spent much of his game in some turmoil against Frederik Svane but held firm for a draw.With Gukesh's win already banked, Praggnanandhaa and Arjun Erigaisi didn't need to force matters either, settling for draws against Vincent Keymer and Matthias Bluebaum, respectively. India closed out the match 2.5-1.5.With the win, India moved to 15 points, still one point behind hosts Uzbekistan, who beat the United States on Friday to stay in front.India's women's team also had a productive Friday, with Vantika Agrawal and Divya Deshmukh both delivering important wins to seal the match against Uzbekistan.Vantika, playing white against Nilufarkhon Imomkuzieva, picked up an early pawn with a sharp tactical sequence; a check with her queen forced Black's king to give up material before the middlegame had properly begun.She nursed that small material edge through a long, technical battle, trading down into a rook endgame where her extra pawn and more active king proved decisive.Pushing her kingside pawns forward in the closing stages, Vantika eventually broke through, and Imomkuzieva had no way to hold the position together.Divya Deshmukh's game against Gulrukhbegim Tokhirjonova was a far longer and more chaotic affair.Both sides grabbed material early. Tokhirjonova's knight snatched a pawn on b7 just as Divya's queen picked up a stray piece on d2, leaving the position roughly balanced but sharp.What followed was a marathon battle through the middlegame and into a complex rook, knight and bishop endgame, with both players navigating tricky technical positions deep into the game.Divya's technique held up better over the long haul, and after 73 hard-fought moves, Tokhirjonova had nothing left to stop Black's advancing king, resigning the position.Those two results were enough to see India through the match, keeping the team firmly in the mix for a medal.As things stand, India's women sit second in the standings on 15 points, behind an in-form Chinese side on 17.With two rounds left, India's hopes of gold now depend largely on whether China slip up, but on Friday's evidence, neither Indian team looks inclined to make things easy for anyone chasing them either.In the Open section, India face Uzbekistan 2, while the women’s team take on China in the penultimate round of the Chess Olympiad.
Article Summary: Dommaraju gukesh beats germany's alexander donchenko in round 9 of the 46th chess olympiad in samarkand, uzbekistan. India's women's team also had a productive friday, with vantika agrawal and divya deshmukh both delivering important wins to seal the match. Tokhirjonova's knight snatched a pawn on b7 just as divya's queen picked up a stray piece on d2.

Article Title: 'Feels like a dream': An Se-young completes badminton's golden sweep with Asian Games triumph over Akane Yamaguchi
Article Text:
Gold medalist South Korea's An Se-young (AP Photo)

An leaves Yamaguchi chasing shadows

South Korea's An Se-young gestures after her win against Japan's Akane Yamaguchi. (AP Photo)

From controversy to another major title

An Se-young added another glittering chapter to her extraordinary career on Tuesday, defeating Japan’s three-time world champion Akane Yamaguchi 21-17, 21-9 to win Asian Games gold and underline her status as the world’s No. 1-ranked female badminton player.The South Korean star has now collected virtually every major prize the sport has to offer. Already a Paris Olympic champion and two-time world champion, An has added a second Asian Games gold medal to her collection, further strengthening her extraordinary claim to the top of the women’s game.An dropped to her knees after sealing victory, before arching backwards and looking skyward in an emotional celebration.“It feels like a dream,” An said. “I am so happy and I'm overwhelmed with emotion as I think back to all the hard work I've put in.”The final was a demonstration of An’s athleticism, court coverage and relentless pressure. She repeatedly used the full width and depth of the court, forcing Yamaguchi into long, exhausting movements before finding openings to finish points.“I decided to approach the match with the aim of making my opponent feel rushed and forcing her to move around a lot,” An said.Yamaguchi, a three-time world champion, struggled to match An’s pace in the second game as the South Korean surged away to a commanding 21-9 victory.An had earlier defeated China’s Chen Yufei in the semifinals, extending her winning streak against her Chinese rival to five matches.An’s journey to the top has also included difficult moments. After winning Olympic gold in Paris, she criticised South Korea’s national training system, saying she had been forced to play through a knee injury and questioning some training methods. She later backed away from her threat to pursue an independent path.But on the court, An’s response has been emphatic. With another Asian Games title secured, the 24-year-old has once again demonstrated why she sits at the summit of women’s badminton.
Article Summary: An se-young defeated japan’s three-time world champion akane yamaguchi 21-17, 21-9 to win asian games gold.
